title: Welcome to AskPearls Developer Center
desc: Learn how to create, publish and maintain DecisionOS recommendation widgets, and discover the wider AskPearls ecosystem.

steps.title: Understand the platform
steps.body: DecisionOS is the current widget product. Build a guided question flow, configure recommendations, publish a version, and embed the widget on a website.

steps.title: Choose your path
steps.body: Business users can follow Portal Walkthroughs. Developers can use Installation and Integration Guides to embed and troubleshoot widgets.

steps.title: Start in the Portal
steps.body: Join AskPearls, create a widget, then work through the builder, decision content and publishing checklist.

notes: The Developer Center is public documentation. Account data and editing remain in the authenticated Portal.

title: Create your AskPearls account
desc: Get access to your personal AskPearls workspace through the Portal.

steps.title: Open the Portal
steps.body: Select Join AskPearls or Open Portal to visit portal.askpearls.com.

steps.title: Authenticate
steps.body: Use the sign-in method provided by the Portal. The current Portal includes Google authentication.

steps.title: Open your workspace
steps.body: After signing in, review the Dashboard and locate Widget Builder or My Widgets.

steps.title: Create your first widget
steps.body: Use the creation flow and select the target website for the widget.

notes: Do not enter account credentials into the Developer Center. Sign-in occurs on the Portal.

title: Your first DecisionOS widget
desc: A complete guided path from a blank widget to a published installation.

steps.title: Create a widget
steps.body: Open Widget Builder and create a new widget or choose an existing draft.

steps.title: Configure appearance
steps.body: Set heading, description, primary and background colors, typography, size and position.

steps.title: Add questions
steps.body: Build the visitor question sequence and test that the options make sense.

steps.title: Add recommendations and rules
steps.body: Configure what the visitor should see for different answers.

steps.title: Save drafts
steps.body: Save the design, question, recommendation and rule drafts as needed.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Open Publish & Embed, complete readiness checks and publish the eligible widget.

steps.title: Install and test
steps.body: Copy the generated snippet, place it on your website, and test on the allowed domain.

notes: Publishing may be blocked until required configuration is complete.
A saved draft is not the same as a published live version.

title: Dashboard walkthrough
desc: Find your widgets, understand their status and move into the next action.

steps.title: Open Dashboard
steps.body: Sign in and select Dashboard in the Portal navigation.

steps.title: Review widgets
steps.body: Check recent widgets, status and summary metrics. Values are tied to the authenticated account.

steps.title: Open an existing widget
steps.body: Select a recent widget or use My Widgets to open it for editing.

steps.title: Create new
steps.body: Use the New Widget action to begin another DecisionOS experience.

notes: Dashboard totals should be verified against your live account; documentation contains no sample production metrics.

title: Manage your widgets
desc: Find, select and maintain widgets in your account.

steps.title: Open My Widgets
steps.body: Use the Portal navigation to open your widget collection.

steps.title: Choose a widget
steps.body: Review its name, target website, current status and version information.

steps.title: Edit
steps.body: Open Widget Builder or Design & Customize for the selected widget.

steps.title: Publish when ready
steps.body: Navigate to Publish & Embed after preparing the widget.

notes: Published widgets and editable drafts can have different version numbers.

title: Widget Builder: basics, appearance and behavior
desc: Configure the visitor-facing experience using the three builder tabs.

steps.title: Basics
steps.body: Enter the widget name and content. Choose the associated target website where applicable.

steps.title: Appearance
steps.body: Adjust primary/background/text colors, font, size, corner radius, width, button shape and theme.

steps.title: Behavior
steps.body: Review display preferences and position, then preview the experience.

steps.title: Save Draft
steps.body: Save your changes. Check the confirmation message and updated draft version before navigating away.

steps.title: Preview
steps.body: Test desktop and mobile appearance before publishing.

notes: Portal builder includes Basics, Appearance and Behavior tabs.
Design draft settings observed in the API include fonts Inter, Arial, Georgia and Verdana, widths 300–520 and positions bottom-right, bottom-left and center.

title: Questions and answers
desc: Design a clear question flow that visitors can complete.

steps.title: Write the first question
steps.body: Use language visitors understand without specialist knowledge.

steps.title: Add answer options
steps.body: Make options mutually understandable; avoid overlapping labels.

steps.title: Order questions
steps.body: Put essential qualifying questions first and optional refinements later.

steps.title: Save question draft
steps.body: Save the draft, then verify the flow by previewing the widget.

steps.title: Test branches
steps.body: Check each relevant answer path before publishing.

notes: Questions are saved separately from some other draft content; check the save status of each section.

title: Recommendations
desc: Define the outcomes DecisionOS can show visitors.

steps.title: Create recommendation entries
steps.body: Give each outcome a clear title and useful description.

steps.title: Explain the benefit
steps.body: Use practical language and avoid claims you cannot support.

steps.title: Connect outcomes to rules
steps.body: Ensure each relevant answer combination leads to an intended result.

steps.title: Save and preview
steps.body: Save recommendation drafts and test the user-facing results.

notes: Recommendation content should match your real products or services, not generic sample copy.

title: Decision rules
desc: Connect visitor answers to relevant recommendations.

steps.title: Identify conditions
steps.body: Choose which answers or combinations should influence the outcome.

steps.title: Set matching behavior
steps.body: Define when each recommendation should be eligible.

steps.title: Check overlaps
steps.body: Review conflicting or incomplete conditions.

steps.title: Test scenarios
steps.body: Try positive, negative and edge-case answer paths.

steps.title: Save draft
steps.body: Save decision rules before publishing.

notes: The precise rule operators available may evolve; use the options shown in your current Portal.

title: Design & Customize
desc: Edit the appearance of an existing widget without confusing draft and live versions.

steps.title: Select the widget
steps.body: Choose the widget you intend to update.

steps.title: Review current design
steps.body: Check heading, description, button text, colors, font and position.

steps.title: Adjust styling
steps.body: Keep colors accessible and check readability in light and dark contexts.

steps.title: Save Draft
steps.body: Confirm the draft version increments or the Portal reports a successful save.

steps.title: Republish when appropriate
steps.body: A new draft does not automatically replace the published version.

title: Publish & Embed
desc: Publish an eligible widget and obtain installation instructions.

steps.title: Select a widget
steps.body: Open Publish & Embed and choose the correct widget.

steps.title: Review readiness
steps.body: Check the content, design and installation readiness indicators.

steps.title: Review domains
steps.body: Add or review the website domains where the widget will be used.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Use Publish Widget when enabled. If disabled, read the reason shown in the Portal.

steps.title: Choose a platform
steps.body: Select Custom HTML, WordPress, Shopify or Wix.

steps.title: Copy the actual embed snippet
steps.body: Use the Copy Code action from the selected widget. Do not substitute an example public key.

steps.title: Verify live
steps.body: Load the site and test a complete visitor interaction.

notes: The Portal contains a publish eligibility guard and a status indicator.
Domain enforcement and verification may depend on deployment readiness; do not treat a saved domain as proof of verification.

title: Allowed domains
desc: Manage the websites associated with a widget.

steps.title: Open Publish & Embed
steps.body: Select the widget whose domains you want to manage.

steps.title: Enter the domain
steps.body: Use the hostname shown in the browser, for example example.com. Follow the Portal input guidance.

steps.title: Add the domain
steps.body: Submit and confirm it appears in the allowed-domains list.

steps.title: Remove an obsolete domain
steps.body: Delete only domains that no longer need to serve the widget.

steps.title: Verify enforcement
steps.body: Test the installation on an allowed website and check the deployment status of domain enforcement.

notes: Adding a domain is not the same as verifying DNS ownership.
The Portal has domain verification-related endpoints, but their production readiness must be confirmed before promising enforcement.

title: Analytics & Activity
desc: Understand widget usage and visitor progress.

steps.title: Open Analytics & Activity
steps.body: Use the Portal navigation to reach the analytics page.

steps.title: Set date range
steps.body: Choose the reporting period appropriate for your question.

steps.title: Filter widgets
steps.body: Focus on a particular widget or compare all widgets if supported.

steps.title: Review metrics
steps.body: Inspect widget views, interactions, completion rate and recommendations.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Use Export CSV when available and validate the downloaded columns before reporting.

notes: Some current Portal markup includes demonstration figures; do not assume those figures represent live account activity.

title: Install on a custom HTML website
desc: Add the widget to a site you control using the exact snippet generated by the Portal.

steps.title: Publish first
steps.body: Make sure the widget has a published version.

steps.title: Copy from Portal
steps.body: Open Publish & Embed, select Custom HTML and click Copy Code.

steps.title: Paste into your page
steps.body: Insert the snippet near the end of the body or in the location specified by the generated instructions.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.body: Publish your HTML changes to the target domain.

steps.title: Test
steps.body: Check browser console and network requests, then complete a full widget interaction.

notes: The snippet below is only a placement example. Copy your real script and attributes from the Portal.
code:
<!-- Existing page content -->
<!-- Paste the exact AskPearls snippet copied from Publish & Embed here -->
</body>

title: Install on WordPress
desc: Use the generated embed code in a WordPress site.

steps.title: Publish and copy
steps.body: In Publish & Embed, choose WordPress and copy the snippet.

steps.title: Choose insertion point
steps.body: Use a trusted custom-code or footer insertion method supported by your WordPress installation.

steps.title: Paste once
steps.body: Avoid inserting the same widget snippet twice through both a theme and plugin.

steps.title: Clear caches
steps.body: Clear any page cache or optimization layer if the script does not appear.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test on a public page, including mobile.

notes: Only use WordPress plugins or theme editing tools you trust.
A native AskPearls WordPress plugin should not be claimed available until released.

title: Install on Shopify
desc: Place the Portal-generated snippet into a Shopify theme where custom code is permitted.

steps.title: Back up the theme
steps.body: Duplicate your current theme before changing code.

steps.title: Copy snippet
steps.body: Choose Shopify in Publish & Embed and copy the current widget snippet.

steps.title: Insert in theme
steps.body: Use the theme code editor or supported custom-code section and place the snippet as instructed.

steps.title: Save and preview
steps.body: Check the storefront preview before publishing the theme change.

steps.title: Test live
steps.body: Confirm the widget loads on relevant pages and does not obscure checkout controls.

notes: Shopify theme layouts vary. Check the active theme and current Shopify restrictions.

title: Install on Wix
desc: Embed the widget using Wix custom code where your plan and editor permit it.

steps.title: Copy snippet
steps.body: Choose Wix in Publish & Embed and copy the widget code.

steps.title: Open custom code settings
steps.body: Locate Wix custom code or equivalent supported site integration settings.

steps.title: Paste code
steps.body: Use the placement and scope recommended by the Portal.

steps.title: Publish the site
steps.body: Changes may not appear on the public domain until the Wix site is published.

steps.title: Test
steps.body: Verify desktop/mobile rendering and any domain-related restrictions.

notes: Custom-code availability and placement rules depend on your Wix configuration.

title: Embed snippet reference
desc: Understand the relationship between your published widget, the loader and the site.

steps.title: Use the generated snippet
steps.body: The authoritative installation snippet comes from the Portal, not from this documentation.

steps.title: Loader location
steps.body: The Portal currently identifies a CDN loader at cdn.askpearls.com/app.widgets/widget.js.

steps.title: API origin
steps.body: The Portal currently identifies api.askpearls.com as the widget API origin.

steps.title: Treat keys as identifiers
steps.body: A public widget key identifies a widget; do not embed authenticated Portal access tokens.

steps.title: Avoid duplicates
steps.body: Include a widget only as instructed and check for duplicate script injection.

notes: CDN paths and loader attributes may change; always prefer the live snippet.
This is an integration overview, not a public API contract.
code:
<!-- Illustrative only; not a runnable widget configuration -->
<script src="https://cdn.askpearls.com/app.widgets/widget.js" defer></script>

title: Widget configuration concepts
desc: Understand drafts, versions, appearance and website targeting.

steps.title: Draft versus live
steps.body: A draft is editable; a published version is the content visitors should receive.

steps.title: Appearance
steps.body: The design can include theme, typography, colors, width, radius, position and button shape.

steps.title: Questions and recommendations
steps.body: Questions collect answers; decision rules select recommendations.

steps.title: Website targeting
steps.body: Associate the widget with the intended website and review allowed domains.

steps.title: Publish changes
steps.body: After editing a published widget, follow the Portal publish process again when required.

notes: The exact JSON schema of internal draft APIs is not a supported public API specification.

title: Security and deployment checklist
desc: Use safe practices when publishing and embedding widgets.

steps.title: Use HTTPS
steps.body: Serve the site and widget assets over HTTPS.

steps.title: Protect Portal credentials
steps.body: Keep authenticated Portal sessions and tokens out of client-side snippets.

steps.title: Review domain settings
steps.body: Configure allowed domains and check whether enforcement is active in your environment.

steps.title: Test content
steps.body: Ensure your questions and recommendations do not request unnecessary sensitive information.

steps.title: Monitor errors
steps.body: Review browser errors and the Portal analytics for unexpected behavior.

notes: Do not treat client-side checks as a substitute for server-side authorization.

title: Public API availability
desc: Separate the internal authenticated Portal proxy from any future external API.

steps.title: Current implementation
steps.body: The Portal uses authenticated routes under /Widget/Api/widgets to manage its own widgets.

steps.title: External integration
steps.body: Use the generated embed snippet for supported website integration.

steps.title: Public API documentation
steps.body: No stable public API contract, credentials flow or versioning guarantee has been verified for third-party developers.

steps.title: Future release
steps.body: When a public API is formally released, this page can publish endpoints, authentication, schemas and examples.

notes: Internal API route names are intentionally not presented as public integration instructions.

title: Troubleshooting guide
desc: Diagnose the most common widget installation and publishing problems.

steps.title: Widget does not appear
steps.body: Confirm the widget is published, the snippet is present once and the CDN script loads successfully.

steps.title: Publish button disabled
steps.body: Read the readiness reason in Publish & Embed; review content, design and installation prerequisites.

steps.title: Widget appears on wrong site
steps.body: Check the target website and allowed-domains configuration.

steps.title: Old design remains visible
steps.body: Confirm the latest draft was published and clear relevant caches.

steps.title: No analytics data
steps.body: Check that visitors are loading and interacting with the live widget and that analytics is enabled.

steps.title: Browser errors
steps.body: Inspect the Console and Network panels for blocked scripts, CSP violations or failed requests.

notes: When contacting support, include the widget public key, page URL, approximate time and a redacted error message.

title: Frequently asked questions
desc: Quick answers about accounts, widgets and the Developer Center.

steps.title: Is Developer Center a separate account?
steps.body: No. The documentation is public. Account management is handled by the Portal.

steps.title: Can I create multiple widgets?
steps.body: The Portal supports multiple widgets; exact limits depend on the active plan.

steps.title: Does Save Draft publish my changes?
steps.body: No. Draft saving and publishing are distinct operations.

steps.title: Is there a free trial?
steps.body: The product plan includes a free tier; do not assume a time-limited free trial.

steps.title: Are all AI agents available?
steps.body: No. DecisionOS is the current MVP; other agents are future plans.

steps.title: Is there a public REST API?
steps.body: A supported public API contract has not been verified for release.

title: Contact and support
desc: Get help with setup, integration and unexpected behavior.

steps.title: Check documentation
steps.body: Use Search or Troubleshooting to find an existing answer.

steps.title: Collect details
steps.body: Record the widget public key, site URL, steps to reproduce and browser information.

steps.title: Use official channels
steps.body: Open the Portal or the published AskPearls support contact channel when available.

steps.title: Protect secrets
steps.body: Never send passwords, access tokens or private customer information in a support report.

notes: Support contact address and ticketing integration must be configured before launch; no unverified email address is displayed.

desc: Our long-term roadmap of connected AI products, developed one by one.

steps.body: Build the next agent based on product readiness and user needs.

steps.title: Status labels
